- Using MOD operator: ST uses MOD? In CODESYS, MOD is allowed. But we have (writeIndex + 1) MOD windowSize; need to ensure writeIndex is INT and windowSize INT, MOD returns INT, assignment to INT OK.
- The logic: when count < windowSize, we store new value at buffer[writeIndex], then increment writeIndex. Once count == windowSize (i.e., full), we go to else branch: subtract buffer[writeIndex] (the oldest), add new, store new, then writeIndex = (writeIndex + 1) MOD windowSize. This is correct circular buffer.
- But note: initial writeIndex starts at 0, count=0. When first value arrives, count<windowSize, store at buffer[0], sum+=value, count=1, writeIndex=1. Second value, store at buffer[1], etc. When count reaches windowSize, writeIndex equals windowSize (since every value increments writeIndex by one, and when count=windowSize, writeIndex=windowSize). Then next value: else branch, buffer[writeIndex] is buffer[windowSize] which is out of bounds because buffer has indices 0..99 and windowSize can be 1..100. If windowSize=100, buffer[100] is out of bounds (valid indices 0..99). This is a bug! Actually when count==windowSize, writeIndex == windowSize, and buffer has size 100, but windowSize could be up to 100, then writeIndex=100 is out of range. But also when count==windowSize, the buffer is full, but writeIndex is currently pointing to the next free slot? The else branch tries to overwrite the oldest. However the oldest is at index 0 initially, not at writeIndex. The algorithm is flawed.

Better approach: maintain writeIndex as the index where the next new value will be written; when buffer not full, write at writeIndex then increment; when full, overwrite the oldest, which is exactly at writeIndex (because writeIndex has been cycling modulo windowSize). To keep it simple: We can maintain a circular buffer of fixed max size 100, but only use windowSize elements. When not full, use writeIndex as insertion point and count increments. When full, we need to replace the oldest. The oldest is at writeIndex as well if we always write at writeIndex and then advance modulo windowSize. But when not full, we don't use modulo; we just write at writeIndex and increment writeIndex. When full, writeIndex should be set to 0 after first full? Let's think.

Option: Always use circular indexing modulo windowSize. Initialize writeIndex=0, count=0. Each new sample:

- else: sum = sum - buffer[writeIndex] + value; buffer[writeIndex] = value; writeIndex = (writeIndex + 1) MOD windowSize;
This works if we initialize writeIndex=0 and always MOD after increment. For full case, buffer[writeIndex] is the oldest because writeIndex points to the next slot that will be overwritten, which after cycling equals the location of oldest. When not full, we can also use MOD but writeIndex never exceeds windowSize. So we can unify: always use MOD on windowSize. However, when count < windowSize, writeIndex < windowSize so MOD not needed but fine.

So fix: use writeIndex := (writeIndex + 1) MOD windowSize; even in the not-full branch. This ensures wrap around.
